name: Save complete GIS engineering data automatically and reopen it
covers: node and link hydraulic attribute preservation
description: Verifies mapped engineering features retain hydraulic and spatial attributes in a named project draft.
steps: Open a project GIS draft
Add a junction and reservoir with coordinates, elevation and demand/head
Add a pipeline and set diameter, roughness, status and explicit upstream/downstream node references
Wait for automatic save confirmation
Reload the GIS workspace and reopen the draft
expected: The same node and pipe specifications, coordinates, hydraulic metadata and endpoint references are restored.

name: Edit CAD entities and preserve layers and drawing units
description: Verifies CAD geometry can be selected, inspected, edited, removed and saved without losing layer metadata.
steps: Create a line and a circle on separate named layers
Select the line and edit its layer or coordinates
Delete the circle using the explicit delete control
Save and reload the project
expected: The edited line and its layer remain saved; only the confirmed selected circle is removed.

name: Import and export GIS and CAD exchange files
description: Verifies supported GIS and CAD exchange workflows preserve supported feature attributes and geometry.
steps: Import GeoJSON containing a point and pipeline with properties
Export the GIS draft as GeoJSON
Bring GIS features into CAD
Export the drawing as DXF
expected: GeoJSON retains feature properties and geometry; supported CAD entities are present in the DXF.

name: Keep independent GIS drafts and require confirmation before deletion
description: Verifies multiple designs remain separate and destructive actions require confirmation.
steps: Create two named GIS drafts with different features
Open the first draft and verify its contents
Cancel deletion of the second draft
Refresh the draft list
expected: Both drafts remain available and unchanged after cancelling deletion.

name: Model individual junction demand patterns, pump energy and generate a design report
description: Verifies junction-specific patterns are transferred to EPANET, pump energy is calculated from simulated flow and head with declared assumptions, and a printable hydraulic report is produced.
steps: Load the example network and select Junction J1
Enter a demand pattern different from Junction J2 and set a 1-hour pattern timestep
Set pump efficiency to 75%, electricity tariff to 30 KES/kWh and operating hours to 12 per day
Run the extended-period EPANET simulation
Review pump average/peak power, simulated kWh and projected daily cost
Download the hydraulic design report and open its print dialog
Export the EPANET INP and confirm each junction has its own pattern assignment
expected: The INP contains distinct pattern IDs assigned to each junction; simulation results show pump energy and cost based on simulated flow/head and the stated efficiency/tariff assumptions; the report contains hydraulic criteria, warnings, node/link results and energy estimates.

name: Connect to the real QGIS Server WMS and WFS project
covers: WFS GeoJSON import into GIS draft
description: Verifies the GIS workspace reads real QGIS Server WMS and WFS capabilities, displays a selected server-rendered layer and imports valid WFS GeoJSON without treating an empty layer as a successful feature import.
steps: Open the GIS workspace and choose Check QGIS services
Confirm the server project reports WMS and WFS readiness and lists the published engineering layers
Select a WMS layer and show its QGIS Server overlay on the map
Select the junctions WFS layer and import features
Verify the interface clearly reports zero features when the published layer is empty
Submit an unsupported WFS type name through the feature query workflow
expected: The UI lists layers advertised by live QGIS Server GetCapabilities responses, the WMS overlay requests tiles from the QGIS project endpoint, WFS returns GeoJSON for an allowed layer, and unsupported layer names are rejected.

name: Process real terrain data with PyQGIS and compare pipeline profiles
covers: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM with GLO-90 fallback
route alternative length and elevation comparison
description: Checks the GIS workspace calls the dedicated PyQGIS service through an authenticated owner-scoped backend route and displays DEM-derived results.
steps: Open a GIS project with a mapped boundary and at least two pipeline alternatives
Run a pipeline ground profile at 30 m sample spacing
Compare the pipeline route alternatives
Generate contours at a 5 m interval and calculate terrain slope
Verify contours appear as GIS line features
Export contours as GeoJSON and pipeline profiles as CSV
expected: The PyQGIS service returns DEM source and resolution, station elevations, ascent/descent and grade values, route comparison ranks, contour GeoJSON and slope class statistics. Only an authenticated owner of the project can invoke the backend terrain route.

name: Check PyQGIS processing service and Copernicus DEM coverage for a project
description: Verifies the authenticated project owner can check the dedicated PyQGIS service and whether public Copernicus DEM tiles are available near the project centre.
steps: Open a project GIS workspace
Add a project boundary or mapped features
Tap Check PyQGIS / DEM coverage
Review the PyQGIS online status and GLO-30/GLO-90 availability for the project centre
expected: The status panel reports the live PyQGIS service and the public DEM tile availability for the project-centre coordinate, including a clear local-GeoTIFF fallback message when no tile exists.
